source.display_title: 05/09/2026 - Luis Jauregui x Farooq Bey  — Undetermined

prospect.name: Cole Carson
prospect.location: Costa Mesa, Orange County, California, USA
prospect.occupation: Youth minister at a church; also a working musician (drummer) who plays gigs
prospect.family_status: Has a daughter turning two in a couple of months; moved house a couple of months ago
prospect.training_background: Long-standing self-directed trainee, 'fairly consistent' but works out only a couple of times a week. Prefers 30-40 minute high-intensity interval sessions using jump rope and kettlebells at home rather than going to a gym. Lost 40-50 lb roughly eight years ago and has kept it off; sat around 175 lb at his lightest, has held ~195 lb for about the last year and a half, targets 185 lb. Used the Ladder app for a year, on and off.
prospect.medical: No medical conditions, injuries or medications disclosed; the rep never asked. Prospect volunteered long-standing hip tightness: 'I've always had pretty tight hips.'

signals: Already training regularly and eating deliberately (intermittent fasting, meal prep) — not seeking rescue
Explicitly frames the goal as exceeding rather than recovering: 'I would love to exceed those expectations, for sure'
Frames it as longevity and function rather than transformation: 'I'm definitely in the longevity game right now... I just want to be super functional and strong'
Confidence held down because price was never discussed — his response to a $6,000 anchor is untested, and the recording ends before any offer

goals.text: Move well and stay functional for the long term — 'I'm definitely in the longevity game right now, like I'm not trying to be like insanely swole or anything, I just want to be super functional and strong'
Get back down from ~195 lb to around 185 lb at roughly 12% body fat
Become genuinely consistent so training is 'just part of the routine' rather than something he hopes he gets to
Improve mobility, particularly chronically tight hips — 'I really want the mobility'
Keep getting stronger via progressive overload — 'I want everything in my body to be strong'
A routine that is sustainable rather than extreme — 'something that isn't insane, that's sustainable'
Carry the momentum into the rest of his life — 'it'll just give me confidence in all the other aspects of my life to go for it more and not just settle on things'
Stay healthy enough to be useful to his daughter and the people he serves — 'if I'm not healthy, what good am I going to be to anybody else?'

pains.text: No external accountability; the sessions he skips are the ones he most needs — 'the ones that I don't want to do are the ones that I really need to do'

Schedule has become unpredictable since his daughter was born and a recent move; mornings are his preference but he is protecting sleep, and evenings are taken by ministry — 'it's kind of finding the windows because it's not the same every day that I have those windows'
Trains only a couple of times a week despite wanting more — 'I always feel better when I'm done working out and I'm not as consistent as I'd like to be'
Feels hard-won progress is eroding; has drifted from 175-185 lb up to a maintained 195 lb — 'like slowly slipping away' and 'I don't want to lose what I've already worked for'
Diet is undermined by the food environment of his job — 'it's really tough around in church, because there's a lot of temptation in ministry, there's always like some sweet treats hanging out'

[proposed label: mobility_restriction] Long-standing hip tightness he attributes partly to drumming — 'I've always had pretty tight hips, I'm a musician and I'm a drummer, so I don't know if that's part of why'

evidence: The recording ends mid-sentence at 00:15:50 while the rep is still deepening goals, so no offer, price, close attempt or next step is observable.
Nothing about money, programme structure or tiers was said at any point in the recorded portion.

Counter-evidence — the prospect was unusually warm and close to pre-sold: 'that's why I kind of felt like this program would be pretty perfect for me' and 'what Trevor has, like, sounds pretty perfect to me', so a close off-recording is entirely plausible.
Counter-evidence — the prospect said the health change was 'definitely a need though', a strong buying signal, before the recording cut.
outcome.next_step: None stated before the recording ends. The prospect twice offered to reschedule because he was driving to a gig; the rep declined and continued.

notable.note: Four things a manager would want. (1) The file title names 'Luis Jauregui' but the person on the call is Cole Carson throughout, addressed as Cole by the rep from the first minute — the prospect identity in the corpus title is wrong. (2) The rep stated the company's policy against taking calls with people who are driving, waived it, and then declined the prospect's own two offers to reschedule, running the whole call while the prospect drove to a gig. (3) The recording terminates mid-sentence at 00:15:50, so most of the process and the entire outcome are unobservable. (4) This is the first call of a pair: the same prospect returns to the same rep on 2026-05-12 (call_id 2026-05-12_cole-carson_farooq-bey, drive_file_id 1PrnnTMGQf-T9xRvQS8gGVVvnOWQFT1cr, titled 'Steven Silbert x Farooq Bey'). That record notes an earlier call it could not identify — this is it. On the second call the rep resets deliberately: 'It's been probably like 15 calls since I last spoke to you. So I don't want to operate under previous assumptions.'

quality.notes: Frequent swaps. At 00:00:07 the block labelled 'Cole Carson' contains the rep's greeting ('Hey, Cole, how's it going?'). At 00:00:41 a single 'Cole Carson' block contains both the question 'Where are you based, dude?' and the answer 'I'm in LA area. I'm in Costa Mesa'. At 00:04:48 and 00:04:59 blocks labelled 'Farooq Bey (Primal Instinct)' are plainly the prospect speaking ('Just me trying to like motivate myself', 'I'll get a couple in'). Role was read from content throughout: Farooq Bey runs every discovery question and is the rep. Poor connection is acknowledged in-call ('I think there's a bit of lag', 'Lost you there for a sec'), which likely contributes.
